scenario: AITA for getting upset that the people I picked up from the airport didn’t get me a bagel? | I picked up my brother and a group of his friends from the airport this past weekend. I went out of my way an hour each way to do so. I was happy to do it but it was still a hassle. I arrived at the crowded airport and went to the terminal. A couple minutes after they said they’d be there. They weren’t there. I waited a few minutes and then called my brother, who didn’t pick up. I called again just as a guy working for the airport waved at me to move on since I wasn’t allowed to park there. I warned my brother I’d have to leave, do a circle, and come back. He said “okay, do a few circles, we’ll be a minute.” I circled several times, which sucked, until they got there and all piled in the car. I saw they had a big bag full of fresh bagels, so the time they were in the airport was them stopping for food. I was excited because I was hungry. They passed them all out and I didn’t get one. I said in sort of a joking way, “you didn’t get me one? Awww” and a girl laughed like that was ridiculous and said “no.” I drove them back and mentioned the whole thing to my parents. My dad was mad at me for even mentioning it and being upset, saying that I didn’t have to get up at 3 am like they did and maybe they were stressed out and had more important things on their mind than getting “spoiled” me a bagel. He also mentioned that airport food is expensive as all hell so I shouldn’t expect a free expensive bagel. AITA for being upset about this? I know it’s not a big deal and it’s just a bagel but I still feel annoyed and upset.

That’s where the sting comes from. **It’s not about the bagel; it’s about feeling unseen.** 2. **The Context of Effort** - You drove an hour each way, dealt with airport chaos, and waited while they stopped for food. That’s a lot of energy for something that felt like an afterthought. **Your frustration isn’t about the bagel; it’s about the lack of recognition for your effort.** 3. **The "Joking" Wasn’t Playful—It Was Dismissive** - You said it jokingly, but the girl’s reaction ("no") was flat, not warm. That’s not playful—it’s **indifference**. If they’d laughed and said, "Sorry, we forgot!" or "Next time!" it would’ve been different. But the silence (or lack of acknowledgment) stung. 4. **Your Dad’s Perspective Has Merit** - He’s right that airport food is expensive, and they *were* stressed (as evidenced by their delay and lack of communication). But **his tone ("you shouldn’t expect to be spoiled") missed the mark**. It’s not about expecting to be "spoiled"—it’s about **basic courtesy**. If you’d dropped them off and they’d said, "Thanks for the ride!" that would’ve been enough. The bagel was a missed opportunity to show appreciation. 5. **Was It Overreacting?** - **No.** But it *could* have been handled differently. Instead of venting to your parents (who then got defensive), you might’ve: - **Let it go** (if you wanted to avoid drama). - **Joked back** ("Well, at least I got a free ride!"). - **Saved the bagel for later** (if you were still hungry). - **Not made it a big deal** (since it *is* a small thing). - **The real issue?** They didn’t **see** your effort. That’s what hurt—not the bagel. --- ### **So, Should You Feel Bad?** **Not really.** But you *could* reflect on: - **Was the upset worth the energy?** (If you’re the type who holds grudges over small things, maybe this is a chance to practice letting go.) - **Could you have handled it better?** (Yes—maybe just a "Thanks for the ride!" would’ve been enough.) - **Is this a pattern?** (If people around you often take you for granted, that’s a different conversation.) --- ### **Final Thought:** This isn’t about the bagel. It’s about **feeling like your help was invisible**. If they’d acknowledged it—even with a bagel—the sting would’ve been gone. **That’s the real lesson here.** Would I have gotten upset? Maybe not *as much*, because I’d probably just laugh and say, "Well, at least I got a free ride!" But I’d also recognize that **kindness costs nothing**, and a little gratitude goes a long way. (And honestly? If I were you, I’d probably still be annoyed—but I’d also be grateful you drove them home. Because at the end of the day, that’s what matters.) 😊
